previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, and glaucoma was admitted for acute onset blurry vision in her left eye, which was her better-seeing eye with only 20% visual acuity and severe peripheral vision loss at baseline. Imaging revealed a small chronic brain infarct but no acute stroke, and ophthalmology suspected worsening proliferative diabetic retinopathy as the cause of vision change. She also presented with uncontrolled diabetes, acute kidney injury, and hypovolemia, likely exacerbated by diuretic use. Her diuretics were held, IV fluids were given cautiously, and her kidney function improved. Blood and urine cultures showed no infection. She was stabilized, educated on symptom monitoring, and discharged with plans for ophthalmology follow-up and medication adjustments.

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF SUMMARY STATEMENT:  Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female a 
history of Type I Insulin Dependent diabetes mellituscomplicated 
by neuropathy, peripheral vascular disease, gastroparesis and 
charcot joint with chronic R ___ metatarsal base ulceration and 
L heel ulcer admitted for worsening diabetic foot ulceration.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
  
# Bilateral Foot Ulcer:  The patient presented from her 
podiatrist's office for concern of worsening infection of her 
chronic foot ulcer.  She had previously been on ciprofloxacin as 
an outpatient without adequate source control.  On presentation, 
she was found to have a fever and leukocytosis (WBC of 13.4).  
Podiatry was consulted who recommended Vancomycin, 
Ciprofloxacin, and Flagyl for treatment of severe diabetic foot 
ulcer infection.  Her prior cultures from recent foot infections 
show MSSA and pan-sensitive Pseudomonas (history of MRSA 
infection ___ ___.  Podiatry performed a bedside irrigation and 
debridement on ___.  A right foot xray was performed which 
showed question of osteomyelitis.  Her ESR and CRP also returned 
elevated with ESR at 111.  She was then taken to the OR on 
___ for surgical debridement.  No evidence of infectious 
involvement of bone was noted  suggesting no active 
osteomyelitis.  The paitent had cultures sent which have grown 
pan-sensitive pseudomonoas.  Given her history of MRSA infection 
as well as a clinical presentation consistent with severe 
diabetic foot infection, the patient was discharged on a three 
week course to end on ___ of doxycycline for MRSA coverage 
(patient has an allergy to bactrim) and levofloxacin for 
pseudomonal and recent group B strep positive coverage.   

# Hyperglycemia and Type 1 Insulin Dependent Diabetes Mellitus:  
The patient is a Chronic Insulin Dendepent Diabetes Mellitus 
Type I, poorly controlled with A1c of 13.1% and complicated by 
gastroparesis, peripheral neuropathy (autonomic dysfunction), 
peripheral vascular disease and charcot joint.  She was admitted 
with poorly controlled blood sugars with critically high finger 
sticks to 600s.  She was treated with intravenous fluids and 
insulin with improvement of her blood sugars.  Given elevated 
blood sugars on admission ___ the setting of a poorly controlled 
type one diabetic, the ___ consult team evaluated the patient 
and recommended some modifications of her home insulin regimen.  
She was discharged with well-controlled blood sugars on an 
insulin regimen including Levemir 10 Units Breakfast, Levemir 5 
Units Bedtime, NPH 30 Units Breakfast, and a insulin sliding 
scale using humalog.  This regimen is near her baseline as the 
patient is slowly regaining her ability to tolerate food intake. 
  

# Acute on Chronic Renal Failure:  The patient was chronic renal 
insufficiency with baseline creatinine of 1.4-2.0 admitted ___ 
acute renal failure with creatinine of 2.3 possibly related to 
hypovolumia ___ setting of hyperglycemia and worsening infection. 
 Her creatinine improved and neared her baseline following 
intravenous fluids and control of her infection.

# Gastroparesis:  The patient has had decreased oral intake with 
some nausea and vomiting ___ the setting of infection and recent 
surgery.  We continued the patient on her home dose of 
omeprazole, zofran, ativan, senna, and colasce for her 
gastroparesis.  We attempted to do use reglan for promotility 
but had little effect.  The patient was able to have a bowel 
movement on the day of discharge following intake of lactulose.  
Recommended that the patient continue lactulose until she 
regains bowel function. 

# Hyponatremia:  Initially found to have pseudohyponatremia with 
sodium of 136 following correction for blood glucose.  Her 
sodium was within normal range at time of discharge. 

CHRONIC ISSUES

# Hyperlipidemia:  Stable.  Continued atorvastatin 80 and 
ezetimibe 10 daily 

# Hypertension:  Initially held her home losartan given acute on 
chronic renal failure and hyperkalemia.  Her potassium returned 
to high normal range and began to trend down.  We restarted her 
losartan on 25mg daily and increased her to her home dose of 
50mg on day of discharge.  

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
1.  Dressing Changes and Podiatry Follow-up:  The patient should 
have saline wet to dry dressing changes daily on both bilateral 
foot ulcers.  She should also have a negative pressure wound vac 
on her right ulcer until she follows up with podiatry ___ 
approximately 1 weeks time.  
2.  Weight bearing status:  The patient can weight bear for 
transfers only on the left forefoot.  She is non-weight bearing 
on her right lower extremity.
3.  Elevated potassium:  The patient's potassium was high normal 
during hospitalization.  It was trending down close to 
discharge.  As such, her losartan was titrated up from 25mg to 
her home dose of 50mg daily.  She should have repeat 
electrolytes drawn within ___ days of discharge.
4.  Blood Sugars:  Your blood sugars were somewhat difficult to 
control during your hospitalization.  The ___ consult service 
evaluated you and determined your most appropriate discharge 
insulin regimen.  Please attempt to follow this insulin scale 
with titrations as necessary.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Patient with Charcot deformity with worsening infection
underlying the fifth metatarsal base.  Evaluate for evidence of osteomyelitis.

COMPARISON:  Multiple foot radiographs, most recent ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Right foot, three views.

FINDINGS:  Compared with prior examination, there is little overall change in
the neuropathic joint with extensive sclerosis, heterotopic bone formation and
architectural disintegration.  Vascular calcification is seen along the dorsum
of the right foot.  A plantar ulcer is identified, with a rim of thickened
soft tissue in the base of the fifth metatarsal, but there is no clear
destructive bone lesion at this level to suggest osteomyelitis. However, in
the lateral view, there is indistinctness of the cortical margin of the
inferior aspect of the calcaneous. Calcaneal plantar spurs as well as an os
trigonum are re-identified.

IMPRESSION:  
1.  Indistinctness of the cortical margin of the inferior aspect of the
calcaneous raises concern for osteomyelitis. Further assessment with MR is
recommended. 
2.  No significant change in neuropathic arthropathy of the mid foot and
plantar soft tissue ulcer.
